title: Lady Viking volleyball season underway | Jackson Star and Herald - Ripley and Ravenswood | wvnews.com
text:
RIPLEY, W.Va. (WV News) - Ripley's Lady Viking volleyball team enters the season of 2025 with momentum, confidence and a summer of hard work behind them.
Ripley was a runner-up at the Tyler Consolidated Summer Tournament before winning the title at the Poca Summer Tournament.
"This year’s squad is anchored by three seniors who bring leadership and experience to the floor," said Craddock.
"(Libero) Delaney Howery is a skilled defensive specialist and consistent server. She was named to the Cardinal Conference Second Team last year.
"Tiffany Fisher returns as a powerful outside hitter and defensive presence at the net." Fisher earned Cardinal Conference Honorable Mention in 2024.
"Jalyn Ramsey provides energy and reliability as a defensive specialist with a strong serve.
“These seniors bring so much experience and game awareness to the court. They’ve stepped seamlessly into their leadership roles.”
The rest of the varsity roster "is loaded with talent," according to Craddock.
Juniors are Dezzie Steele, Kaydence Sheppard, MacKenzie Durback, Kate Burdette, Braylinn Lutz and Addyson Taylor.
Lutz earned All-State Honorable Mention
and Cardinal Conference Second Team recognition last year. Taylor earned Cardinal Conference Honorable Mention last year.
The sophomore class features Kira Huffman, Willow Simon,
and Addison Howery.
Lilly Cirst is the lone freshman on varsity.
The junior varsity roster features freshmen Elaina Rake, Kinsley Cooper, Payton Westfall,
Chelsea Lewis and Ava Casto.
"Crist, Durback and Huffman are expected to split
time between JV and varsity," Craddock noted.
"With a strong mix of veteran leadership and young talent, we are prepared to
compete at a high level (in 2025). The bar is set, and expectations are clear: this team is ready to
chase championships."
Ripley defeated Chapmanville, 25-12 and 25-13. Howery anchored the defense with nine digs. Howery and Steele had three aces. Offensively, Fisher stood out with seven kills and a .462 hitting percentage. Fisher and Lutz each had seven kills. Setter Kaydance Sheppard added 10 assists.
Ripley lost to South Charleston, 25-21 and 25-16. Lutz and Fisher each had six kills. Sheppard added nine assists. Howery was the defensive leader with 10 digs.
The Lady Vikings headed to St. Albans for a tri-match and got revenge on South Charleston, 25-21 and 25-15. Howery had three aces while Fisher and Lutz each had 10 kills. Sheppard contributed 15 assists. Howery had 15 digs and 20 receptions.
Ripley fell in three sets to St. Albans, winning the first, 25-21, before dropping the final two, 25-16 and 15-10. Lutz had 12 kills, Steele finished with two aces, and Sheppard recorded 14 assists. Howery once again paced the defense with 10 digs and 16 receptions.
Ripley was part of a home tri-match with Point Pleasant and Roane County. Ripley defeated Point, 25-22 and 25-20. Howery led the attack with nine kills and a .615 hitting percentage. Lutz served two aces and Howery had 18 digs. Willow Simon delivered 12 assists.
Ripley later defeated Roane, 25-12 and 25-16. Simon and Lilly Crist each had three aces. Fisher had six kills. Simon also had nine assists with Sheppard delivering eight. Crist had 10 digs.
Ripley's junior varsity won two matches over Chapmanville and Point.
